name: P2P Stream
description: Stream torrents straight into Jellyfin. Built-in torrent sources (no extra software), TMDB catalogs as libraries, search for any movie or show from the Jellyfin search bar, and Burst-style quality filters.

versions.changelog: Playing away from home works without a setting: each device is given stream links using the address it reached Jellyfin by (the home address at home, your reverse proxy's address away from home). Devices at home are unaffected if the outside address is turned off. A fixed address can still be set under Stream links.
Fix: when a user asks to play a title they can't access, the plugin no longer searches for it or starts a torrent (it now checks library access, not just parental ratings). Tidier log messages.

Security and reliability release. New: option to hide the search libraries from the home screen while keeping them in search. Stream links shown to apps no longer include the stream token; making a new token is done on the server, with an option to stop old links at once, and rewriting links is much faster. Playback only answers for titles the user can see. Links from search results and torrents can't reach your home network, and .torrent downloads are size-limited. Searches set to use the proxy never fall back to a direct connection. Each torrent downloads into its own folder. Catalogs sharing a folder no longer remove each other's titles, and catalog collections only change collections the plugin made. Season packs play the right episode file. Plus fixes for subtitle files, Trakt sign-in, the torrent limit, cache sizes and setting descriptions.

Pre-loads the next episode, playback safety fixes for season packs and subtitle files, subtitles for torrents you add, Trakt without a Client Secret, and removing unused catalog folders. See the release notes.
First stable release: on-demand torrent streaming with built-in sources, catalogs, Version menu, fast starts, release subtitles, VPN privacy and port forwarding. See the release notes.
The log says, once per release, how many subtitle files it had (or why none were added).
Subtitle files that come with a release (.srt, .ass, .ssa, .vtt) are offered in Jellyfin's subtitle menu, labelled by language (Playback > Faster start, on by default).
